reviews.review: Constant, bloody, fast-paced action. All the weapons feel great, and there can be tons of enemies on screen at a time. Runs great, too. If you're looking for something a little light on story and set pieces, but heavy on action, look no further than this gem.

As a long-time fan of the Warhammer 40,000 universe, I was excited to delve into Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine - Anniversary Edition. This action-packed, third-person shooter truly captures the brutal and gritty essence of the 40k universe.

The Anniversary Edition includes all previously released DLC, along with enhanced graphics and improved performance. The visual updates are noticeable, making the world of the Space Marines even more immersive and detailed. The game runs smoothly and the controls are responsive, which is crucial for the fast-paced combat this game is known for.

The gameplay itself is where Space Marine truly shines. As a genetically enhanced super soldier, players will find themselves in the midst of intense battles against the forces of Chaos. The combat is incredibly satisfying, with a wide variety of weapons to choose from and brutal execution moves to dispatch your enemies in style. The game does a fantastic job of making you feel like a powerhouse, mowing down enemies with ease.

The campaign is engaging and well-paced, with a thrilling storyline that will keep you hooked until the very end. The voice acting is top-notch, and the sound design really adds to the atmosphere of the game. Additionally, the multiplayer mode offers hours of intense, fast-paced action that will keep you coming back for more.

Overall, Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine - Anniversary Edition is a must-have for fans of the 40k universe and action-packed shooters. With its improved graphics, smooth gameplay, and engaging storyline, this game is a worthy addition to any gamer's library. Highly recommended.

Multiplayer wasn't terrible - not great either - but the single player campaign was a blast.  Did enjoy the few games of the horde mode I managed back in the day too.

Melee combat is extremely satisfying and the ranged weapons are very 40K inaccurate (in terms of their firing accuracy, not their feel).

Some great little (and not so little) environmental details add to the atmosphere.
